core.title: Feedback-loop must close the loop
core.given: A feature is marked kind: feedback-loop.
core.when: You author or revise its plan artifacts and acceptances.
core.then: Declare at least one smoke acceptance with a close_the_loop block containing both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.
prefer: Define success as all three: (a) producer detected a condition and emitted a correction, (b) consumer received and reacted (consumer_reacted), and (c) the producer's predicate no longer fires next cycle (drift_resolved).
avoid: Acceptances that stop at 'producer emitted a correction' without proving the consumer reacted.
Proving the consumer reacted without proving the drift is gone on the next cycle.
A close_the_loop block missing either required field, or placing it on a non-smoke acceptance.
core.why: A feedback loop only works if the correction is consumed and the triggering condition disappears; emission alone proves nothing about the loop closing.
evidence: The feedback-loop feature has at least one acceptance of smoke type whose close_the_loop block contains consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.
The stack's convention check for this rule reports no finding for the feature.
verification: Scope gate: the rule applies only when the feature's kind is feedback-loop; any other kind is not applicable. Path, file-kind and task-term facts — including the profile's plan-artifact location and filename patterns — are retrieval hints only, never gates; the source imposes no path or task-word restriction.

Require at least one smoke acceptance carrying a close_the_loop block; the stack's validator for this rule reports a finding for a feedback-loop feature otherwise. The validator and finding ids are realization details. Any acceptance-ID shape shown in the realization is an illustrative example, not a required pattern; the stack's generic smoke-acceptance identification shape, if one exists, belongs to the profile, not to this rule.
Term close_the_loop = the required smoke-acceptance block for a feedback loop; required fields: consumer_reacted and drift_resolved; both must be present.

Success semantics: (a) producer detected a condition and emitted a correction, (b) consumer received and reacted, AND (c) the producer's predicate no longer fires next cycle (drift resolved). Field presence alone does not satisfy success if the acceptance proves only producer emission.

fires: A feature of kind feedback-loop is authored or edited and has no smoke acceptance at all.
A feedback-loop feature has a smoke acceptance but its close_the_loop block is missing, or lacks consumer_reacted or drift_resolved.

A feedback-loop feature's close_the_loop block lists both fields, but the acceptance only proves the producer emitted a correction (not that the consumer reacted and the predicate stops firing next cycle).
doesNotFire: Feature whose kind is anything other than feedback-loop.

Feedback-loop feature with at least one smoke acceptance whose close_the_loop block contains consumer_reacted and drift_resolved AND whose acceptance proves all three parts of success: correction emitted, consumer reacted, drift no longer fires next cycle.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the stack's plan artifacts (the feature definitions this rule scopes) live, used only as a retrieval hint — never a gate — when locating feedback-loop features and their acceptances.

The stack's local name for the plan artifacts in which the feature's plan and acceptances are authored, so 'plan artifacts and acceptances' instantiates to the Bun 'plan, WMBTs and acceptances'.

No naming preference is added to the core, which would otherwise strengthen the rule; bun.json is delivered as the reference example.

bunOnly.reason: Only the requirement (at least one smoke acceptance carrying a close_the_loop block) is stack-neutral and moves to core verification; the illustrative acceptance-ID example stays in the realization for the same reason as prefer[0].

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral: it governs the ATDD plan-artifact schema (feature kind feedback-loop, smoke acceptance, close_the_loop block with consumer_reacted and drift_resolved), which is shared across stacks, so those tokens are kept verbatim rather than abstracted away; the capitalized Bun token 'SMOKE' is rendered as the neutral 'smoke acceptance'/'smoke type'. Per feedback, three fixes were applied: (1) the illustrative acceptance-ID example (acc:<wagon>:<wmbt_id>-SMOKE-NNN-close-the-loop) is no longer a core naming preference nor the stack-wide urn.smoke_acceptance profile value — the Bun input establishes no generic smoke-acceptance URN shape, so the example stays in the realization (bunOnly) as explicitly illustrative and no preference is added; (2) layout.feature_dir is no longer used; the retrieval globs are split into roles.plan_artifact.path ('**/features/**') and suffix.plan_artifact ('**/*feature*.yaml'), both hint-only; (3) the core's prefer retains only the three-part success definition. The plan-artifact local name (WMBT) moves to profileRequirements; only the validator/finding id (planner.smoke.feedback-loop-close-the-loop) is genuinely bunOnly. No new profile keys were needed, so proposedKeys is empty.
